lines.text: Do you know how video calls work? Your face crosses the planet in a fraction of a second, thirty times every second.
Raw video is huge. Just one second of HD would take well over a hundred megabytes. Far too much for most internet connections.
So the codec only sends what changes. Your wall doesn't move, so it's sent once. Your mouth moves, so that part is updated.
The picture is cut into small blocks. Each frame mostly says, this block moved a little that way. That shrinks the video by a hundred times or more.
Then it's chopped into small packets, and sent over the internet. Each one can take its own route.
Some arrive late. Waiting would freeze the call, so video calls usually skip a lost packet and keep going. That's the glitchy face you sometimes see.
In a group call, everyone sends one stream to a server, and the server forwards it to the others. Otherwise your phone would have to upload to every person.
Orbi Transfer has rooms too. Make a private Space with a name and a code, and everyone who joins sees the same files, wherever they are.
